# @eltonbautista/vue

Cabinet is a small, playful Vue 3 component library with an arcade-cabinet feel and a tested accessibility contract on every component.

**Components:** `CabButton`, `CabTextField`, `CabCheckbox`, `CabSwitch`, `CabSelect`, `CabTabs`, `CabDialog`, `CabCard`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @eltonbautista/vue @eltonbautista/tokens
```

```ts
// main.ts
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/tokens.css'   // design tokens (CSS custom properties)
import '@eltonbautista/tokens/fonts.css'    // Sora + Outfit (optional)
import '@eltonbautista/vue/style.css'       // component styles
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { CabButton, CabTextField } from '@eltonbautista/vue'
const email = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <CabTextField v-model="email" label="Email" type="email" />
  <CabButton>Book a seat</CabButton>
</template>
```

## Accessibility

Every component follows a WAI-ARIA APG pattern and documents its keyboard map, focus behaviour and screen-reader output. Each one is tested in a real browser for keyboard interaction and axe violations. See the Storybook docs for each component's Accessibility section.

## For AI assistants

The landing page is in `src/App.vue` and `npm run build` passes with no errors. I did not check it in a browser, so the keyboard flow, focus moves and axe results are unverified.

**What's on the page**
- **Title and intro:** an `h1` and a short intro.
- **Tracks:** three `CabCard`s linking to `/tracks/board`, `/tracks/digital` and `/tracks/larp`. The card's `href` stretches the link over the whole card, so a click anywhere on it navigates.
- **Sign-up form:** name, email and experience level (a select), plus a code-of-conduct checkbox. Submitting with missing or invalid fields shows a summary that takes focus and lists each problem. Per-field errors appear and update live once you've tried to submit.
- **Confirmation:** a valid submit opens a `CabDialog` showing the details, with "Confirm booking" and "Go back and edit". Nothing is booked until you confirm.
- **Email reminders:** a `CabSwitch` that saves on change and announces "Saved" in a status region. There is no save button.

**Choices I made that you may want to change**
- **Code of conduct blocks submit through validation, not a disabled button.** The button stays enabled and shows the error. A disabled button gives no reason why it's unavailable.
- **Reminders default to off** and persist in `localStorage` under `workshop.emailReminders`. There is no backend in this project.
- **Booking is a TODO.** Confirming only switches the page to a "Your seat is booked" message. No request is sent.
- **Code of conduct has no text or link.** The workshop's CoC document wasn't provided, so the checkbox label is the only reference to it.

**Things to know**
- The track pages don't exist yet, and there's no router, so the card links are plain `href`s. Until those pages exist they will 404.
- I didn't add vue-tsc, Playwright or axe to this project, so type-checking and the WCAG 2.2 AA check were not run. Keyboard behaviour, focus return after the dialog closes, and the stretched-link click target all need a browser pass.
- The build created a `dist/` folder in the project.
